question: How was the cell discovered by Robert Hook?
solution:
The correct answer is __**By observing cork**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Robert Hooke discovered the cell in **1665** when he was examining a thin slice of cork under his microscope.
 
• He observed small, box-like structures which he termed as "**cells**" because they reminded him of the small rooms in a monastery.
 
• The cork cells observed by Hooke were actually **dead plant cells**.
 
• His discovery marked the beginning of **cell theory**, a fundamental concept in biology that states that all living organisms are composed of cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microscope**

 
 
• A microscope is an instrument used to see objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye.
 
• Robert Hooke used a compound microscope, which has two sets of lenses for magnification.
 
• Microscopes are essential tools in biology for studying cells and microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Cell Theory**
 
 
• Cell theory is a fundamental principle in biology that states that all living organisms are composed of cells.
 
• It was developed in the 19th century by scientists like Matthias Schleiden, Theodor Schwann, and Rudolf Virchow.
 
• The theory has three main points: all living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.
 
 
 
• **Cork**
 
 
• Cork is a natural material obtained from the bark of cork oak trees.
 
• It is composed of dead cells that form a protective layer for the tree.
 
• Cork is lightweight, buoyant, and impermeable, making it useful for various applications, including wine bottle stoppers.
